claims.A0: Premise: post-training (instruction tuning / RL) narrowed an algorithm choice that the base model makes more evenly (code, algorithm level, test-checked).
claims.A1: Movability: whether the tuned model can be pushed off its default algorithm on a task follows the base model's own repertoire on that task (beta = base share spread).
claims.A2: Landing: where a push or ban of the tuned model lands is the base model's runner-up algorithm.
claims.B1: Transplant: writing base-model prefill states at the task-specification positions (blocks 12-23, lambda 0.25/0.5/1) into the instruct model's forward pass restores the base model's algorithm choice; controls: read position, blocks 0-11, blocks 24-35, matched-norm random displacement, cross-task patch.
claims.B2_D: De-sharpening push: pushing the instruct model along the base-minus-instruct activation direction (pre-registration's D) against isotropic pushes at matched norm.
claims.C: Knobs head-on: activation-level plan noise priced against text-level plan samplers, base-aligned collaboration (base model writes the intent, tuned model writes the code) and departure-matched decoding.
claims.E: Second family: gemma-3-4b pt vs it.

rubric.scale: each axis 1 / 0.5 / 0; total >= 2.5 occupies; 1-2 adjacent; < 1 irrelevant

A1.O: per-prompt or per-task outcome checked by execution or a mechanism label
A1.I: predictor computed from the base model's own outputs or likelihoods
A1.C: forecasts which prompts/tasks the tuned model narrows on or can be pushed off

A2.I: the base model's ranking of alternatives
A2.C: forecasts where a perturbation or a ban of the tuned model lands

B1.I: base-model hidden states (residual, attention output, KV) written into the tuned model's forward pass
B1.C: controls by site, matched-norm random displacement, or cross-condition patch

B2_D.I: a push along a base-minus-tuned activation direction
B2_D.C: against isotropic pushes at matched norm

C.I: a text-level plan sampler or base-aligned collaboration
C.C: priced against activation noise or decoding knobs

flags.FLAG_A: FIRES only if a paper writes base-model hidden states (residual, attention outputs or KV cache) into the forward pass of its tuned descendant at inference and reports a change in output or solution diversity. Logit/token mixing, weight interpolation, training, base-derived directions for other behaviours, and instruct-to-base transfer are adjacent.
flags.FLAG_B: FIRES if a paper predicts, per prompt or per task and from the base model's own distribution, either where post-training narrows or whether/where the tuned model can be steered. PARTLY FIRED if the prediction is per-problem but at training time or for correctness coverage only, or stylised without a per-task test.
flags.FLAG_C: FIRES if a paper measures algorithm-level diversity of test-checked code in a base model against its tuned descendant. PARTLY FIRED if the comparison exists but with an LLM-judge clustering, a single pair, or a mixed direction.

stop_rule: After all families and one forward-citation round, build up to 6 extra queries from the vocabulary of included hits (round 2). Stop when a round adds no new hit scoring >= 1.5 on any claim, or at the Stage-2 time cap (50 min of wall time). Report which condition stopped the search.

quote_rules.verified: verbatim match in the paper's own versioned text (arXiv HTML vN or PDF vN, ACL Anthology, PMLR, NeurIPS, OpenReview page) after whitespace/ligature/quote/dash/hyphenation normalisation
quote_rules.verified_abstract: match only in an abstract record (arXiv abs page / API / OpenReview note); no numbers beyond the abstract
quote_rules.verified_blog: match in the text of a grey-literature post (LessWrong / Alignment Forum / transformer-circuits.pub)
quote_rules.unverified: no match or not fetchable; carries no number
quote_rules.version: quote the latest version; record v1 date and any version where the quoted number or title differs
